wychhazel: The wych-elm; -- so called because its leaves are like those of the hazel.
wynn: One of the runes adopted into the Anglo-Saxon, or Old English, alphabet. It had the value of modern English w, and was replaced from about a. d. 1280 at first by uu, later by w. X. | A kind of timber truck, or carriage.
wynd: A narrow lane or alley. [Scot.] Jamieson. The narrow wynds, or alleys, on each side of the street. Bryant.
wychelm: A species of elm (Ulmus montana) found in Northern and Western Europe; Scotch elm. Note: By confusion this word is often written witch-elm.
wyandots: Same as Hurons. [Written also Wyandottes, and Yendots.]
wye: 1. The letter Y. 2. A kind of crotch. See Y, n. (a).
wyla: A helmeted Australian cockatoo (Calyptorhynchus funereus); -- called also funeral cockatoo.
wyn: One of the runes adopted into the Anglo-Saxon, or Old English, alphabet. It had the value of modern English w, and was replaced from about a. d. 1280 at first by uu, later by w. X.
wyclifite: A follower of Wyclif, the English reformer; a Lollard.
wycliffite: A follower of Wyclif, the English reformer; a Lollard.
